t: Winning Sequences: DP on (Last Move, Score Difference)
o: Bob must pick a sequence with no two consecutive equal moves and finish with strictly more points than Alice. Alice's moves are fixed by s. Each round contributes −1, 0, or +1 to (Bob − Alice): +1 if Bob's creature beats Alice's (W>F, F>E, E>W), −1 if it loses, 0 on ties. We need the number of Bob sequences ending with a positive difference. With n ≤ 1000, DP over rounds × last move × difference (offset into [−n, n]) is only ~9·10⁶ states/transitions.
k: Only the score *difference* matters, and it changes by exactly −1/0/+1 each round, so it fits in a [−n, n] array with an offset.
The no-repeat rule means the DP state must include Bob's previous move (3 options).
Beat relations form a cycle: W beats F, F beats E, E beats W; encode as a 3×3 table of +1/−1/0.

a.i: dp[last][d] = number of Bob prefixes ending with move `last` and current difference d (Bob minus Alice, offset by n). Initialize with round 0 choices; transition to a different move b each round adding beat[b][alice]. Sum dp[*][d] for d < 0 (offset) at the end.
s: Map F/W/E to 0/1/2 and fill the beat table.
Seed dp[b][offset + beat(b, s[0])] = 1 for each opening move b.
For each subsequent round, for each last move and each new move b ≠ last, add dp[last][d] into nd[b][d + beat(b, a)].
Sum all dp[b][j] for j < offset modulo 1e9+7.
a.t: O(n² · 9) — n rounds × (3 last moves × 3 next moves × 2n+1 differences); ~10⁷ operations for n = 1000

w: This DP is the intended solution; a top-down memoized version is equivalent. Pitfalls: getting the beat-cycle direction right (Water beats Fire, Fire beats Earth, Earth beats Water — note it is *not* rock-paper-scissors order), remembering the strict inequality (sum only d < 0, ties don't count), enforcing b ≠ last, and the modulo. Edge cases: n = 1 (Bob wins with the single beating move). Follow-ups: count sequences with a margin of at least k (shift the threshold), or make Bob's first move fixed.
